methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort study of 254 NMIBC patients with complete clinical and pathological data. Appropriate statistical methods: Mann-Whitney U test, Kaplan-Meier analysis, log-rank testing, multivariate Cox proportional hazards models. ROC curve analysis with Youden index for cutoff determination. Subgroup analyses with interaction testing properly conducted. Internal validation with 1000 bootstrap resamples. Minor: retrospective design with acknowledged selection bias.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort study establishing GLR as novel independent prognostic biomarker for NMIBC recurrence after TURBt. Direct clinical relevance: GLR is simple, cost-effective, and easily calculated from routine preoperative laboratory tests. Nomogram provides practical tool for preoperative risk stratification to guide follow-up intensity and adjuvant therapy decisions. Findings support clinical practice change potential.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive reporting of inclusion/exclusion criteria, clinical variables, statistical methods, and outcomes. STROBE compliance evident with baseline characteristics, univariate/multivariate analysis, and subgroup testing clearly documented. Nomogram methodology transparent with C-index, calibration curves, and DCA reported. However, no statement regarding patient-level data or biobank availability for external validation.

novelty_literature.justification: First study to evaluate GLR in NMIBC prognosis; GLR previously validated in other cancers (pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, hepatocellular carcinoma, oral cancer). Conceptual novelty moderate but application-specific to NMIBC is novel. Integration into nomogram with clinicopathological factors (tumor size, number, grade, stage) provides incremental methodological contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: Excellent clarity and organization with strong motivation, comprehensive methods section, systematic results presentation, and thoughtful discussion. Extensive acknowledgment of potential confounders (adjuvant therapy balance, alcohol consumption) strengthens interpretation. Limitations transparently discussed including single-center design, BCG underutilization, unmeasured confounders. Figure quality high; readability excellent.

key_strengths: Novel application of composite biomarker (GLR) integrating metabolic stress and immune status; superior ROC performance (AUC 0.716) versus NLR (0.552) and PLR (0.535)
Rigorous multivariate analysis with appropriate confounding adjustment; robust across clinicopathological subgroups without significant interactions
Comprehensive nomogram incorporating six independent prognostic factors with excellent discrimination (C-index 0.785) and calibration; validated with 1000 bootstrap resamples
Transparent reporting of potential biases and methodological strengths; excellent discussion of biological mechanisms linking GGT and lymphocytes to recurrence risk
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design limits generalizability; requires multicenter prospective validation before routine clinical implementation
GLR associated with recurrence-free survival but not overall survival (P=0.33); specificity for local recurrence versus systemic outcomes needs clarification
Small sample for high-risk subgroups (n=75 with recurrence); statistical power may be limited for interaction testing
No external validation cohort presented; model performance on independent dataset unknown
chief_reviewer.rationale: Strong Tier 3 manuscript with solid methodology, novel biomarker, and practical clinical tool. Retrospective design and single-center nature prevent higher tier placement. Accept with confidence for appropriate journal level.
